checked.claim: EUR 1.25m; TCAS 1 Aug 2025 dismissed appeal, EUR 738,000 after time-barred offences; Sept 2026 ruling cut it to EUR 463,700 after 42 more offences dismissed (party newspaper, not confirmed)
checked.evidence: The cited 'Avante' page is not the PCP newspaper: it is a WordPress.com blog ('Avante Mundo'), and it is internally inconsistent (says the fine became final in January 2026, yet reports a September 2026 ruling). The reduction itself is confirmed by mainstream outlets: CNN Portugal (10 Sept 2026) reports the Central Administrative Court South set the fine at EUR 463,700 after partly upholding the council's appeals, with offences time-barred; the council's lawyer said appeal periods were still running but the council would not appeal. Same story in Renascença, Euronews, JN, Jornal Económico, Correio da Manhã. The '42 offences' figure appears only in the blog and is dropped. DN (5 Aug 2025) confirms the 1 August 2025 ruling: 46 offences time-barred, 65 remained, EUR 738,000. CNPD fine was January 2022.
checked.replacement: The CNPD fined Lisbon City Council EUR 1.25 million in January 2022 for sending personal data of anti-Putin protest organisers to the Russian embassy and other entities. On 1 August 2025 the Central Administrative Court South dismissed the council's appeal but, with 46 offences time-barred, the fine stood at EUR 738,000. In September 2026 the same court partly upheld the council's further appeals and set the fine at EUR 463,700 as more offences had lapsed; the council said it would not appeal further.

checked.claim: Public bodies may ask for a three-year waiver (Art. 44(2)), decided case by case after a charge
checked.evidence: Art. 44(2): public entities could ask for the waiver 'durante o prazo de três anos a contar da entrada em vigor da presente lei'. The law entered into force in August 2019, so the window closed in August 2022. The file presents it as a current option. Deliberation 2019/495 (3 Sept 2019) confirmed: request only after a charge, case by case.
checked.replacement: Yes: fines apply equally to public and private entities (Art. 44(1)), with no special cap. Art. 44(2) let public entities ask for a waiver of fines only during the first three years after the law entered into force (until August 2022), and the CNPD considered requests only after a charge, case by case (Deliberation 2019/495). Courts have confirmed fines on public bodies (Lisbon municipality).
